# Best home backup power stations under $1,000

For most homes, I'd get a 2 kWh LiFePO4 unit. It can run a fridge, a router, and a CPAP for roughly a day, according to the reviewers below. Prices change often, so check the price at checkout.

## Top picks

**1. Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, best if you may want to expand later (about $900)**
- It has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W output, a 10 ms UPS switchover, and takes an add-on battery pack to reach 4 kWh. ([Outage Authority](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup))
- Its 5-year warranty and 800W solar input are also pluses. ([Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/), [Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/))
- Buy: [Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 on Amazon, via Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/)

**2. BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, most battery for the money, with a price caveat ($899)**
- It has 2,074 Wh, 2,600 W output, and a 6,000+ cycle LiFePO4 pack. It is not expandable.
- Dealectric lists it at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-home-backup-power-stations-under-1000-2026-reviews-price-battery-capacity))
- Outage Authority says Bluetti's own price went back to $1,199 after a promotion ended, though Amazon had it at $798.99 on Oct 7. ([Outage Authority](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)) Only buy it if you see it at or under about $900.
- Buy: [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)

**3. BLUETTI AC200L, expandable alternative ($899)**
- It has 2,048 Wh, expands to 8,192 Wh, and includes a TT-30 RV outlet. It is rated for fewer cycles (3,000+) than the Elite 200 V2. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-home-backup-power-stations-under-1000-2026-reviews-price-battery-capacity))
- Buy: [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)

## Smaller and cheaper options

- **Anker SOLIX F1500 ($599.99):** 1,536 Wh with a UPS function. Compare Power Stations tops its value ranking with it and flags the price as unusually low. ([source](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/)) I couldn't get a direct purchase link for it from these results.
- **BLUETTI AC180 ($499):** 1,152 Wh and 1,800 W. It has the best Wh per dollar under $500, but no expansion port. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-home-backup-power-stations-under-1000-2026-reviews-price-battery-capacity)) Buy: [BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 ($489 at Outbound Power):** 1,070 Wh and the lightest at 23.8 lb. It gives about 12 hours for a fridge, CPAP, and router, and solar input is limited to 400W. ([Outage Authority review](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2))
- **ALLPOWERS P1800 ($439, or $395.10 with code ALLPOWERS26):** 1,024 Wh and 1,800 W. It has only a 24-month warranty, and the US product page contradicts itself on some specs. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-home-backup-power-stations-under-1000-2026-reviews-price-battery-capacity)) Buy: [ALLPOWERS P1800](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh)

## How to choose
- **Overnight outages only:** the AC180 or Jackery 1000 v2 is enough.
- **A day or more, or a possible multi-day outage:** get a 2 kWh unit. The C2000 Gen 2 is my pick because you can add capacity later.
- **Well pump, central AC, or 240V:** none of these will cover that, and you would need to spend well over $1,000.

The Dealectric and Outage Authority/Outage Outfitter links are affiliate links, and the reviewers say they haven't lab-tested the units. Specs come from the manufacturers.
